question: Distinguish between shares and debentures of a company.
sources: Companies Act, 2013, definitions of share and debenture
Standard accounting principles for company accounts (ICAI Foundation syllabus)

points.label: Ownership vs debt
points.description: A share is a part of the company's share capital and the holder is an owner (member); a debenture is an acknowledgement of a debt, and the holder is a creditor of the company.
points.basis: Companies Act, 2013, definitions of share and debenture

points.label: Return
points.description: Shareholders get dividends, which are paid only out of profits and are not fixed; debenture holders get interest at a fixed rate whether or not there are profits.
points.basis: Accounting principle: dividend is an appropriation of profit, interest is a charge against profit

points.label: Voting rights
points.description: Equity shareholders have voting rights and a say in management; debenture holders have no voting rights, as a company may not issue debentures carrying voting rights.
points.basis: Companies Act, 2013, voting rights of members and prohibition on debentures carrying voting rights

points.label: Security and repayment
points.description: Shares are usually not secured and share capital is repaid only on winding up (except for buy-back or redeemable preference shares); debentures are usually secured by a charge on assets and are repaid after a fixed period.
points.basis: Accounting principle: redemption of debentures and share capital

points.label: Priority on winding up
points.description: On winding up, debenture holders are repaid before shareholders.
points.basis: Accounting principle: order of payment on liquidation
